full_name: FOCAL — Foundations of Cooperative AI Lab, Carnegie Mellon
mission: 'Our goal is to create foundations of game theory appropriate for advanced, autonomous AI agents – with a focus on achieving cooperation.' Led by Vincent Conitzer (who also holds a role at Oxford), FOCAL studies how AI agents that can copy themselves, read each other's code or simulate each other should reason and cooperate, and how social choice can guide alignment. Founding year approximate ('a new lab').

key_work.title: Foundations of Cooperative AI
key_work.plain_summary: Conitzer & Oesterheld's agenda: game theory built for humans doesn't fit AI agents, so new foundations are needed for AI cooperation.

key_work.title: Social Choice Should Guide AI Alignment in Dealing with Diverse Human Feedback
key_work.plain_summary: Argues that combining many people's feedback (as in RLHF) is a voting problem and should use social-choice theory.

key_work.title: Foundations of Cooperative AI course (Spring 2025)
key_work.plain_summary: A graduate course covering FOCAL's research directions.

people.role: Lab director; professor of computer science, CMU

warnings.text: Advanced AI agents may fail to cooperate, with costly conflict, because classical game theory was not built for agents that can copy, simulate or verify one another.
Aggregating diverse human feedback naively can produce alignment targets that don't represent people fairly.

recommendations.text: Develop game-theoretic foundations tailored to AI agents to make cooperation achievable.
Use social-choice methods when combining human preferences to align AI.
